items.title: `str::substring` that splits a UTF-16 surrogate pair diverges between the backends: `"😀".substring(0, 1)` is half a pair on JS and the whole emoji natively, while `len()` is 2 on both
items.kind: bug (std str; backend divergence on surrogate halves)
items.discussion: lane std-56 (post-Order 55), seen in its url probe: JS strings are UTF-16 and `substring` cuts a code unit; the native str is UTF-8 and its substring rounds to the code point; `len()` reads 2 on both (the UTF-16 count is the language's), so the index arithmetic agrees and the answer does not
items.body: The native backend's `substring` must answer what JS answers at a surrogate boundary (the language's string is UTF-16-indexed: `len()` says so), i.e. a lone surrogate half, which the native str cannot hold as UTF-8 - or the language rules that a cut inside a pair is refused/rounded on BOTH backends (a spec question: strings.md). Rec: find every `str` operation that takes a UTF-16 index (`substring`, `char_at`, `index_of`'s answers, slicing) and pin them on the differential at a surrogate boundary; rule the semantics once (rec: a cut inside a pair answers U+FFFD-free: the half as JS does is unrepresentable natively, so the honest rule is the code-point rounding on both, which changes JS). Owner question. Sizing S-M.
